summary: Emily Ratajkowski's M Le Monde photo shoot drew backlash from plus-size models and activists after she posed standing in one leg of oversized low-rise jeans to show a size gap. Critics called the image fatphobic and out of touch, especially given her book My Body and past comments against body-shaming. The article also cites data on the lack of plus-size representation in fashion and the size of the plus-size market.
one_line: Emily Ratajkowski faced criticism from plus-size advocates over an M Le Monde shoot in which she posed in jeans double her size.
key_facts: Emily Ratajkowski, 32, shared images from a photo shoot with M Le Monde magazine, photographed by Oliver Hadlee Pearch.
In the second image, Ratajkowski wore low-rise, wide-leg denim jeans double her size and stood in one leg of the pair while holding up the waistband.
The shoot was styled by Charlotte Collet and creative directed by Jean-Baptiste Talbourdet-Napoleone.
Thousands of Instagram users criticised Ratajkowski and the team, calling the image "out of touch" and "fatphobic".
Plus-size models and advocates including Tess Holliday, Kelly Augustine, Stephanie Yeboah, Letticia Munniz and Sarah Chiwaya called out the photo.
Tess Holliday commented that she had been looking for those jeans in the second photo and asked Ratajkowski to return them.
Sarah Chiwaya called the second photo "godforsaken trash" and wrote "In the year of our lord 2023?? STILL???"
Ratajkowski has published a book of essays titled My Body about feminist empowerment and the objectification of women's bodies, which made many people surprised by the shoot.
Ratajkowski had not commented on the backlash as of publication; The Independent contacted her representatives and M Le Monde.
In 2019, Ratajkowski defended a friend against body-shaming trolls after a bikini post promoting her swimwear line, Inamorata.
Vogue's Business Size Inclusivity Report found only 0.6 per cent of looks in the autumn/winter 2023 fashion season were modelled by plus-size people.
Future Market Insights expects the plus-size clothing market to reach $288bn in 2023.
Tess Holliday told Elle UK in 2019 that she wears fast fashion and high street to major red carpet moments because high-end options are unavailable.
